thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: ephemeral-storage alert on node gpu-17. Multiple serve pods evicted and restarted in last 6m. Paging #incidents and on-call.

alice-oncall: I’m on it. seeing repeated Evicted events on serve-prod pods. Any customer-facing errors yet? @eva-support could you check front-door errors?

eva-support: Yes — spike in 502/504s for a subset of requests to /v1/generate. Affected customers: two Dedicated tenants in eu-west. Working on incident channel with them, telling them we’re investigating.

ben-runtime: Uploading quick logs: (kubectl describe shows)
```
Events:
  Type     Reason       Age   From     Message
  ----     ------       ----  ----     -------
  Warning  Evicted      4m    kubelet  Pod was evicted: The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage.
```
Also seeing CUDA init errors in the crashed pods logs after eviction when container restarted: `cudaInit failed: out of memory` — likely because model cache rebuild on restart fills /tmp and then native OOM for CUDA alloc.

alice-oncall: Ok so cascade: eviction -> restart -> model cache warm -> disk fill -> runtime crash (cuda oom). Great. Any quick mitigation to stop loop? Need to avoid warm rebuilding while disk is near full.

dinesh-eng: Quick mitigation: mark node unsched, cordon gpu-17, and move remaining pods off. Also increase eviction threshold by patching kubelet config? Not safe mid-incident. Better: delete modelcache dir on node to free space, then restart kubelet? Can we remote-shell and rm -rf /tmp/model_cache/* on gpu-17?

ben-runtime: We can ssh. Running `du -sh /tmp/model_cache` shows ~210G used. Logs under /var/log/serve also ~40G — looks like log rotation failed. If we purge old models and compress logs we recover space quickly.

alice-oncall: @dinesh-eng go ahead with manual cleanup, but be careful. Paste commands you’ll run.

dinesh-eng: Running:
```
ssh root@gpu-17
systemctl stop kubelet
rm -rf /tmp/model_cache/* /var/log/serve/*.old || true
journalctl --vacuum-size=200M
systemctl start kubelet
```
I’ll start with `du -sh /tmp/*` and `ls -lh /var/log/serve | tail -n 20` before deletes. Posting ETA ~5-8m.

eva-support: Notifying affected customers: they see degraded latencies and intermittent 502s, we’ve opened incident bridge and given ETA to me.

incident-bot: New annotation: incident severity P1. Channel: #incidents. Link: https://redwood/incident/1841592653

carmen-sre: I’ll take second pair of eyes. Once the node is cleaned, we should cordon temporarily and migrate critical pods to remain available. Also consider pausing model cache rebuild on restarts — temporarily set ENV SKIP_CACHE_WARM=true for serve pods in that node group.

ben-runtime: Good idea. We can patch the deployment for the node-group to set SKIP_CACHE_WARM=true via a node selector rollout:
```
kubectl -n serve patch deploy serve-runtime --patch 'spec: {template: {spec: {containers: [{name: "serve", env:[{name:"SKIP_CACHE_WARM",value:"true"}]}]}}}'
```
That will apply cluster-wide though; we should limit to the node-group with nodeAffinity if possible — but fast patch is cluster-level until we confirm.

alice-oncall: Prioritize freeing disk first. dinesh, confirm when done and don’t restart any serve pods until we patch SKIP_CACHE_WARM.

dinesh-eng: Cleanup done. Freed ~280GB (removed stale cache & rotated logs). Node free space now ~350G. Rebooting kubelet now.

ben-runtime: Kubelet started, pods coming up. I’m patching deploy to set SKIP_CACHE_WARM=true now to prevent mass warm rebuilds. Will monitor GPU memory during initial requests.

carmen-sre: I’m shifting traffic off gpu-17 via service routing in case of flapping. Also creating canary with SKIP_CACHE_WARM=false on a single pod to validate behavior before reverting cluster-wide.

eva-support: Customer update sent: "We’ve mitigated the disk pressure issue and are routing traffic; we expect degraded behavior to clear in ~15m. We will follow up with RCA and mitigation timeline." They acknowledged, appreciated the quick update.

ben-runtime: Watching logs: no immediate cudaInit errors on new pods. Metrics show latency slowly returning to baseline. 502 rate dropped to normal for affected tenants.

alice-oncall: Good. Handing off active incident to @carmen-sre for postmortem and follow-up actions (log rotation fix, model cache TTL, node alert thresholds). I’m stepping off pager in 20m.

carmen-sre: Taking over. Immediate action items I’ll own:
- Create CRON job to vacuum /tmp/model_cache older than 24h on GPU nodes.
- Add kubelet eviction soft threshold at 15% free ephemeral-storage and alerting to SRE.
- Ensure logrotate config for /var/log/serve is enforced.
- Work with product to consider SKIP_CACHE_WARM rollout and safer cache-warm strategy.

dinesh-eng: I’ll open a PR for the cleanup systemd timer and a helm patch for SKIP_CACHE_WARM node-scoped rollout.

alice-oncall: Thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated. Will leave incident record and meeting notes for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident state changed to MITIGATED by alice-oncall. Metrics snapshot saved to https://redwood/metrics/1841592653

carmen-sre: Filing postmortem, assigning owners and timeline. Will include customer impact summary and follow-up tasks.

eva-support: Customers notified of mitigation and next steps. Closing customer updates after PM review. :thumbsup:
